item: every graceful stop stops the background jobs before the first disposal, and a job past the deadline can no longer write after it (R689)
key_paths: src/safety/shutdown.py; src/safety/uninstall.py; src/database/after_shutdown.py; src/database/writer.py; src/database/session.py; src/database/repair.py; src/config/kv_store.py; src/jobs/background.py; src/llm/concurrency.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; src/api/main.py; tests/test_shutdown_refuses_straggler_jobs.py
summary: BEFORE: the in-app power button (and the update, memory-guard and data-volume stops, all through request_shutdown) and the uninstall's stop disposed the engine BEFORE signalling, so on the stop path people actually use the pool was closed while the collector and the background jobs were still writing; they reopened it, the lifespan's stop-all came after, and its own disposal read EARLIER_DISPOSAL. And a job the 5 s stop-all gave up on (the LLM bulk queue checks its flag only after a whole generation, the Insights backlog between 300-article batches) kept writing after the disposal, because Engine.dispose() only empties the pool and the next checkout opens a fresh connection. NOW: the stop threads no longer dispose; the signal runs the lifespan's one order (scheduler stop, stop-all, the database closed to jobs, write-back, disposal). When the wait ends, whatever it found, src.database.after_shutdown closes the database to jobs: the threads of the jobs still running (by name), any bgjob-* thread (so a job a still-served request starts after the wait), the helper threads such a job runs its work on (run_concurrent's oo-llmbatch pool, through inherit()) and the manual collection pass (oo-scrape-now) with its oo-collect workers (inherit() again; a helper of a helper is followed too, and a pool thread reused later carries no refusal). On those threads every SQLAlchemy statement, commit, write-gate acquire and settings write raises WriteAfterShutdownRefused, logged once per job by its kind; a refused commit never reaches the driver, and every statement is refused too, which matters: with a savepoint the session's commit first sends RELEASE SAVEPOINT, which pysqlite's legacy mode makes the real COMMIT (tested: an INSERT that reached the driver is followed by a refused commit, or by a refused RELEASE, and leaves 0 rows and the gate free). A write queued for the write gate, or waiting on a restore's settings hold, when the database closed is checked again once it gets through; a ROLLBACK statement is let through so a refused job unwinds; the repair job (raw file work) stops before its swap, recorded as stopped (a fresh copy is discarded and made again at the next start, a resumed one is kept). Every other thread is untouched and the next start reopens it. A stop that skips the lifespan's shutdown (a second Ctrl-C during the drain) closes the jobs out and disposes in an exit hook. WAITS for the jobs: power button, update, memstop, data-volume guard's stop, uninstall, Ctrl-C/SIGTERM. Does NOT wait: the panic wipe (deliberately: it destroys the key at once); the data-volume restart after reconnect (execve, nothing disposed); a second Ctrl-C (exit hook, no wait); Windows console end (~5 s). Stated limits: raw DBAPI cursors (incremental vacuum, hygiene) run no SQLAlchemy event; a settings write already past the gate (not one that waited) can still commit; DuckDB is not covered; non-registry threads (import queue, re-index managers, backup threads, rollup builders, request-bound AI streams, and the scheduler's own oo-scheduler thread, whose stop gives up after a 10 s join, with its oo-collect pool, oo-briefing-bg and oo-housekeeping-lane) keep their own stops. Release line: Stopping the app from its power button now lets background jobs finish their current step before the database closes, and a job that is still running then can no longer write to it after the close.
